key_insight: SequenTx couples a virtual-cell simulator with reinforcement learning to design sequential drug regimens that anticipate and steer therapy-induced tumor evolution, producing adaptive schedules that reduce emergence of resistant cell states.
problem_solved: Static, one-size-fits-all treatment schedules fail as tumors dynamically evolve under therapy; this work provides a computational framework to plan multi-step treatments that account for changing cellular-state distributions and resistance trajectories.
method: Build a virtual-cell-inspired simulator that models dynamic cellular-state transitions and population-level tumor evolution under different drugs.
Train a reinforcement learning agent to select time-ordered drug actions that optimize long-term control objectives (e.g., minimize resistant states, maximize progression-free time).
Evaluate learned policies on evolving simulated landscapes and compare outcomes (tumor burden, resistant fraction, time-to-progression) against static and heuristic schedules.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SequenTx is a concrete example of applying RL to nonstationary, mechanistic simulators—highlighting methods for sequential decision-making under evolving distributions and offering a testbed for robust policy learning in high-stakes biomedical settings.
visual_elements: Tumor landscape diagram: state-space of cellular phenotypes with evolving trajectories and agent action arrows
Pipeline flowchart: virtual-cell simulator → RL agent training → policy → clinical treatment schedule

Performance chart: survival / time-to-progression curves comparing learned vs. baseline schedules
paper_title: Reinforcement learning-based design of sequential drug treatment targeting the evolving tumour landscape with SequenTx
paper_authors: Xiaohan Chen, Yue Deng, Xingbo Yang, Ying Zhang, Yuting Huang
